misconception_description: Student believes that modifying a for loop variable inside the loop body does not affects the next iteration's value.

solutions.generated_code:
program PanjangKataTerpanjang
kamus
  n, i, panjangMax, panjangSekarang : integer
  kata : string
algoritma
  input(n)
  panjangMax <- 0
  for i <- 1 to n do
    input(kata)
    panjangSekarang <- panjang(kata)
    if panjangSekarang > panjangMax then
      panjangMax <- panjangSekarang
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endfor
  output(panjangMax)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes they can "skip ahead" to the next element when the current word is shorter than the current max by reassigning the loop variable i. They think this will cause the loop to check that next element instead, optimizing the function. However, modifying i inside the loop body has no effect on what value i will take in the next iteration - the for loop will continue with the next element from list1 regardless. This can cause a runtime error (IndexError) if the same word appears multiple times in the list, since list.index() returns the first occurrence, potentially leading to incorrect index calculations. The student genuinely believes this is an optimization that skips unnecessary comparisons.
